jobs.title: Assistant Professor - HVAC
jobs.description: Assistant Professor - HVAC 494037 Rathdrum HVAC Trades and Industry Full-time Faculty $51,059 - $73,397 Bring your HVAC expertise into the classroom and help prepare the next generation of skilled HVAC professionals. As an Assistant Professor - HVAC, you’ll put your industry knowledge to work through hands-on lecture and laboratory instruction, student advising, and practical learning experiences that connect classroom concepts to the field. You’ll also help maintain the equipment and laboratory environment students rely on to develop their skills. You’ll teach assigned HVAC courses using in-person, online, and interactive delivery methods, drawing on your industry experience to create relevant and engaging learning experiences. You’ll select learning resources, develop course materials and syllabi, assess student learning, and use results to strengthen instruction. You’ll stay current with HVAC technology, equipment, software, and industry practices while maintaining the required industry certification. The role also provides opportunities to work with industry advisory committees, contribute to curriculum and program development, support student recruitment, and build relationships with employers and community partners. You may mentor adjunct faculty, participate in college committees and professional development, and teach evenings or weekends as needed. We’re looking for an experienced HVAC professional who brings strong technical knowledge and a passion for sharing that expertise with others. The ideal candidate can translate real-world experience into effective classroom and laboratory instruction, communicate clearly with students and colleagues, and use technology to support learning. A positive, helpful approach and commitment to student success are essential. Whether you’ve taught before or are ready to take your industry experience into the classroom, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact on the next generation of HVAC professionals. Required License and/or Certifications: Journeyman level status, Industry Certification, or Certification/Licensure by passing a State or Certification/Licensure examination. Must achieve related Idaho CTE Postsecondary Limited Occupational Specialist Certification within first 12 months of employment. jobs.title: Assistant Professor/Program Director – Medical Lab Technology
jobs.description: Assistant Professor/Program Director – Medical Lab Technology 494038 Coeur d'Alene Health Professions Education Full-time Faculty $89,625 - $109,609 Lead a respected Medical Laboratory Technology program while preparing the next generation of laboratory professionals. As the Assistant Professor/Program Director - MLT, you’ll provide academic and program leadership for the Idaho Consortium for Medical Laboratory Technology Education (ICMLTE), ensuring students receive high-quality education and clinical experiences while the program maintains its NAACLS accreditation. You’ll oversee the day-to-day administration and coordination of the program, including accreditation compliance, reports, site visits, program evaluation, curriculum review, student learning assessment, and program planning. You’ll build and maintain relationships with clinical laboratories and healthcare organizations, coordinate clinical affiliation agreements and student onboarding requirements, and work with consortium institutions and clinical partners to support strong learning experiences. You’ll lead advisory and executive committee meetings, contribute to budget planning, support faculty development, coordinate adjunct faculty needs, and participate in student recruitment and admissions activities. You’ll also teach assigned Medical Laboratory Technology courses, provide academic advising and laboratory supervision, and use a variety of instructional methods and technologies. We’re looking for a Medical Laboratory Science professional with knowledge of education, program administration, and NAACLS accreditation requirements. The ideal candidate can lead across multiple institutions and build effective relationships with faculty, students, clinical partners, and other stakeholders. Strong communication, curriculum design and evaluation, training and presentation skills, and proficiency with instructional technology are essential. This role offers an opportunity to combine clinical laboratory expertise, education, and program leadership to make a lasting impact on students and the healthcare workforce. Enjoy excellent benefits, including retirement 2 personal days per year 11 sick days per yearTuition assistance Job Description linked below: (some job boards may not include active links so please click Apply Now on the NIC website or go to www.nic.edu/jobs to see full details); Asst Professor - Program Director MLT.docx Minimum Qualifications• Master’s degree required. • A minimum of three years full-time equivalent experience in medical laboratory science education, including teaching courses, conducting and supervising clinical laboratory learning experiences, evaluating student achievement, providing input into curriculum development, policy and procedure formulation and evaluation of program effectiveness required. Required License and/or Certifications: • Must hold a Medical Laboratory Scientist credential for generalist laboratory professionals from the ASCP Board of Certification. • Eligible to obtain an Idaho post-secondary Career Technical Education (CTE) certificate. • Must have valid driver's license. North Idaho College does not have a vaccine requirement. However, many of our nursing and health professions, are subject to federal or local hospital vaccine requirements. jobs.description: Become an Online Instructor Apply for Online Instructor Openings View current online teaching openings and apply today! Get Involved Apply for Online Academic Support Staff Openings View online openings that do not require a master's degree. Get Involved View the Online Course List Learn more about BYU-Idaho's online courses. Get Involved Add Yourself to Job Posting Alerts Receive notifications for new online job postings. Get Involved Why become an online instructor? At a university that is part of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, our instructors have the unique opportunity to offer testimony and gospel perspective while sharing expertise in their discipline. Many who teach for BYU-Idaho, Ensign College, and BYU-Pathway Worldwide do so out of a desire to give back and bless the lives of future generations. Teaching online is ideal for those who value a flexible work/life schedule. Instructors have the flexibility to schedule those hours around their other obligations. Pay starting at $1,250 per load hour Load hours are dependent on credits/class and if grading assistance is provided. Instructors with a master's degree or higher are compensated at a rate of $1,350 per load hour, while those with a bachelor's degree receive $1,250 per load hour. Additional related duties (leadership, course improvement, training, etc.) may be offered as needed with compensation ranging from $1,400 to $1,610 per load hour. No benefits are offered besides access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP). Curriculum Online curriculum is pre-developed by BYU-Idaho and Ensign College content experts with the help of instructional designers. Typically, instructors do not do live video lectures. Instructor Requirements Online instructors are employees of OLL Services LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of BYU-Idaho which is supported and guided by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Online instructors employed by the LLC are expected to support the missions, values, and standards of the institutions to which they are assigned to teach. All employees are required to agree to maintain the standards of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints as defined by the Church Educational System Honor Code. They guide students to become capable disciple leaders in their personal and professional lives. Ecclesiastical Clearance Hold and be worthy to hold a current temple recommend with the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Education Master’s degree or higher (unless otherwise stated in the job posting). Field Experience Work experience in a related field is preferred. Teaching Experience While online and/or classroom teaching experience is helpful, it is not necessary. "Central to the effort of CES is our mission to develop disciples of Jesus Christ who are leaders in their home, in the Church of Jesus Christ and in their communities. No institutional decision is more important to us than the selection of employees, including faculty, as it has the greatest potential to impact our students." Elder Clark G. Gilbert, Commissioner of Church Educational System Please Note: Current part-time employees of any entity of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints may not teach online in addition to their current employment. Retirees of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints entities are not eligible as it negates retirement benefits.
